title: Care Management and the Individualised Care Plan for Special Needs Plans Members
content:
Every member of a Special Needs Plan has an individualised care plan built from a health risk assessment, and the plan's approved model of care sets how that is done.

## 1. The deadline for the first assessment

> The first health risk assessment is completed no later than the assessment deadline counted from the coverage effective date of the enrollment.

The clock starts from the coverage effective date the enrollment record holds, and the length is the number of calendar days the member's package in the Special Needs Plans category fixes for a first assessment. Calendar days are counted from the day after the coverage effective date, every day of the week counts, an assessment completed on the final day is in time, and full 24-hour periods are never used in place of calendar days. The comparison is not-later-than, and equality at the boundary satisfies it. The condition is tested on the enrollment record, matched to the enrollment the assessment is recorded against, before the assessment is recorded, and on what that record holds.

### The boundary, on hypothetical dates

Counting from the day after the coverage effective date, for the number of calendar days the package fixes:

- An assessment completed on the final day of that count is in time, the final day being inside the deadline.
- An assessment completed on the day after that final day is not in time.
- Days at weekends are counted no differently from days in the working week, and the coverage effective date itself is not counted, the count beginning on the day after it.

## 2. The annual assessment and the review frequency

The assessment is repeated each year within the package's annual assessment days, and a member who moves to a different risk band is reviewed on the frequency their new band calls for rather than the old one.

The days since the last assessment are counted from the date of the most recent completed assessment through the handling date inclusive; where there has never been a completed assessment they are counted from the coverage effective date.

## 3. Reaching the member

The care team makes the package's number of attempts to reach a member before recording them as unreachable, and each attempt is recorded on its own so that the history shows what was tried. The attempts standing to the current assessment cycle are those recorded as attempted with the member not reached, from the start of that cycle through the handling date inclusive.

## 4. A member who declines

A member may decline care management without losing any benefit of the plan, and a declined assessment is recorded as declined rather than left looking overdue.

## 5. After an inpatient discharge

A member discharged from hospital is reviewed within the package's transition days, because that is when things most often go wrong.

## 6. Care management is a benefit

Care management is a benefit and never a condition: no claim is ever refused because an assessment is outstanding.
